head: 91c955ddf20b6699240581289fd68eea7e64334f
summary: This attempt answers the obligations the reworked design and critique put on build. It changes no app code, hook or StallRig. The only file on the staleness list that changed is SmbRig.cs, where two comments now say "per sign-in session" instead of "on this machine". That leaves the person's N-001..N-004 pass at eafb1c3 valid, because the new staleness rule names SmbRig.cs's new content blob as its one exemption. I merged the two SL-038 rule blocks in .taad/fitness.yaml into one. I kept the eng/**/*.ps1 entry and restored the drive and file guards to the stopping-wording rule. The namespace ban in that rule is now a content pattern, because the import-rule form had left eng/rules-harness unable to measure anything (exit 2). The harness now measures again: 40/40 rows AS-RECORDED, including 8 new plants into SL-038's rules. I added case-named StoppingWaitTests, the uppercase-prefix sweep shape, and a default-run tests/window/HookCases.ps1 (H-001, H-002) for the armed-hook shapes. SL-020-scanner.md now records the staleness rule, the StallRig --wait-sec contract, the sweep criterion, and the deferred faulted and self-finished endings. The default suite passes 155/155, C-006 and H-001/H-002 pass, and Fitness passes 25 rules. N-001..N-004 and StalledShareTests remain for a person to run.

files.why: The engine had appended design 2's rules as a second SL-038 block next to build 1's, which gave 28 rules with duplicates. I merged them into one block of 5 entries. Rule 1 is the stopping wording with its drive and file guards back, plus the design's clock and DispatcherTimer patterns. The namespace ban is now a content pattern. Rules 2 to 4 keep design 2's text. I kept the eng/**/*.ps1 entry (O-034).
DIVERGENCE-CLOSED is now reported only for rows from divergences.json. A plant into a settled rule expects xUnit quiet and Fitness fire, and when Fitness misses, that must read MISSED-BY-FITNESS.

S01-S08 plant into SL-038's settled rules. S01-S03 are _scanTask.WaitAsync, Task.WhenAny and the Task.Run(...).WaitAsync chain, which must fire. S04 is the allowed running.WaitAsync, which must stay quiet. S05-S08 are a System.IO using, DriveInfo, File.Exists and Stopwatch.StartNew in StoppingWait.cs. I updated the _note to match.

I replaced three facts with case-named tests. UnderTheGateNothingIsShown (C-013) is a Theory over MinValue, -5 s, -1 ms, 0, 1.999 s and 2 s minus 1 tick. FromTwoSecondsTheLineCountsUpInWholeSeconds (C-014) checks the inclusive 2 s gate, flooring and a never-decreasing count, sampled every 7 ms up to 90 s. FromNinetySecondsThereIsNoEstimate (C-015) checks 89.999 s, 90 s, one hour, TimeSpan.MaxValue and every 997 ms up to an hour.
I added the \\127.0.0.1\FSA0123abcd shape, which must be kept, and stated in the doc comment that the test runs the sweep's own predicate (O-037, C-022).

Comments only: two lines go from 'on this machine' to 'per sign-in session'. RigLock.MachineName is not renamed. The file goes from blob d2e3435d... (eafb1c3) to 8fdf6e87345668eafc91b09015bdf83997820801, the blob the staleness rule names as its one exemption.

Default-run armed-hook cases on a local tree, with no SMB. H-001 (C-020): an armed close decides on ScanningPanel, so it closes while the scan runs and refuses after a fast local Cancel. H-002 (C-026): a marker that never appears (refused after 60 s), stop with no Cancel delay, and an armed throw are all refused with the reason. It loads WindowCases.ps1's helpers by name, so WindowCases.ps1, which is on the staleness list, is untouched.

Records five things: the person-run network check and its staleness rule, with the full path list and the one exemption named by blob (O-033); the sweep's one-predicate criterion and its kept shapes (O-037); StallRig's --wait-sec contract, with its 150 s default, bound and exit codes (O-036); the faulted and self-finished endings as deferred and untested (O-017); and HookCases.

obligations.how: Corrected in this record and in SL-020-scanner.md, with no code change. O-008 is partly tested, not discharged. The faulted and finished-on-its-own endings are deferred: they rest on the single finally, the shipped exe has no seam to produce them, and the 'no test seam' rule forbids adding one. The cancelled ending with the line on screen is owed to the person-run N-001, because C-006 returns in 12-15 ms and never shows the line.

StoppingWaitTests.UnderTheGateNothingIsShown is a Theory over TimeSpan.MinValue, -5 s, -1 ms, 0, 1.999 s and 2 s minus 1 tick. Every row asserts null, so no count can be shown, negative or otherwise. Its filtered command passed 6/6.

StoppingWaitTests.FromTwoSecondsTheLineCountsUpInWholeSeconds checks the exact 2 s wording (inclusive gate), flooring at 2.999 s and 59.999 s, and every 7 ms from 2 s to under 90 s. At each step it asserts the pinned text, a non-decreasing whole-second count and 'Closing the window quits at once.' Its filtered command passed.

StoppingWaitTests.FromNinetySecondsThereIsNoEstimate checks 89.999 s and 90 s minus 1 tick (still the 'minute or more' wording), then 90 s, 90.999 s, 3600 s and TimeSpan.MaxValue (no estimate, no overflow), then every 997 ms from 90 s to an hour. Its filtered command passed.

The test is N-001 (WindowCases.ps1, CheckWaitLine), command `WindowCases.ps1 -Case N-001 -IncludeNetwork`. Under the design's contract only a person runs it, and I did not run it. The person's pass at eafb1c3 stays valid under the new staleness rule, because the only changed listed path is SmbRig.cs at the named exempt blob.
C-006 (`WindowCases.ps1 -Case C-006`) passed again: returned 13 ms after Cancel, a final line at shutdown, detail '-' and the title 'Stopping...' on every line.
The test is N-002, command `WindowCases.ps1 -Case N-002 -IncludeNetwork`. It is person-run and was not run by me. The pass at eafb1c3 is not made stale by this attempt.

tests/window/HookCases.ps1 -Case H-001 passed on a local tree. With no Cancel pressed, the hook closed while the scan ran (scanning=True): window gone 81 ms after Close, process 107 ms, exit 0. After a fast local Cancel (returned in 15 ms), the hook logged 'refused mode=close reason=the scan was no longer running', closed nothing, and the window stayed open.

SmbRigTests.OnlyTheRigsOwnMappingsAreSwept runs LoopbackShare.IsRigMapping, the predicate the sweep calls, over 16 shapes. The new one is \\127.0.0.1\FSA0123abcd, which must be kept. The others include the person's \\100.109.48.75\collab, 7 and 9 digits, non-hex, 127.0.0.2, 127.0.0.10, localhost and --1.ipv6-literal.net. 16/16 passed.

The mapping-level tests are N-003 and N-004, person-run with `-IncludeNetwork`; I did not run them, and their pass at eafb1c3 stays valid. At lock level, the default-run SmbRigTests.ASecondRunWaitsForTheFirst and ALiveHolderFailsTheNextRunLoudlyAndAKilledOneDoesNotBlockIt both passed. The second kills a holder process with TerminateProcess and gets no abandoned-mutex signal, so only the sweep recovers its leftover.

The test is StalledShareTests, command `eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj --filter Network=SMB-LOOPBACK`. It has NEVER run on the extracted rig, by me or anyone. It is person-run under the contract and remains owed to the person.

Plant rows S01-S04 in eng/rules-harness/plants.json feed the real engine's Fitness. `harness.py --scenario plants --only S01,S02,S03,S04` passed 4/4: _scanTask.WaitAsync, Task.WhenAny and the Task.Run(...).WaitAsync chain fire, and running.WaitAsync(token) stays quiet. A mutation run with the WhenAny pattern removed reported MISSED-BY-FITNESS, and the yaml was restored to the same hash.

tests/window/HookCases.ps1 -Case H-002 passed. A marker that never appears is refused 60.2 s after launch with 'did not appear within 60 s, so the stall never armed'. Stop with no delay is refused with 'armed stop needs FSA_HOOK_CANCEL_DELAY_MS'. An armed throw is refused with 'throw mode is not armed'. In all three nothing was pressed, closed or thrown, and the app was still running.

The staleness rule is now written in SL-020-scanner.md. Any change, since the pass HEAD, to any listed path makes the pass stale, and `git diff --name-only` decides with no 'comment-only' judgement. The list: MainWindow.xaml, MainWindow.xaml.cs, StoppingWait.cs, App.xaml.cs, src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/**, the hook, StallRig, all of WindowCases.ps1, SmbRig.cs, StalledShareTests.cs, the Core.Tests csproj and eng/read-window.ps1. The one exemption is SmbRig.cs at blob 8fdf6e87..., the comment-only rewording made here, with MachineName not renamed. I verified that SmbRig.cs is the only listed path changed since eafb1c3.

The eng/**/*.ps1 entry is kept as 'only the shared rig changes SMB client mappings (PowerShell, eng)', with the same patterns as the tests/**/*.ps1 entry. I grepped eng/ for all six patterns and found no hits. Fitness passes.

Rule 1 again bans System.IO, System.Windows and Microsoft.Win32 namespaces, \bDriveInfo\b and \b(?:Directory|File)\.\w+\(, alongside the design's clock and DispatcherTimer patterns. Its 'because' carries the spike 3 reason. Path is not added, per the disposition. Harness plants S05-S08 prove the guards fire. The namespace ban is a content pattern instead of must_not_import; see deviations.

The contract is stated in SL-020-scanner.md: `StallRig.exe --marker <file> [--wait-sec <n>]`. The default is 150 s (LoopbackShare.WaitForOtherRun), so every wait is bounded. On timeout it exits 1 without mapping, with the TimeoutException naming Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig. Bad arguments exit 2. There is no code change, and N-003 is unchanged, as the disposition says.

The criterion is written in SL-020-scanner.md. The sweep deletes only what the single predicate LoopbackShare.IsRigMapping matches: \\127.0.0.1\ plus a lower-case 'fsa' plus 8 hex digits in either case. The default-run test calls that same predicate over every other shape and must keep each one. The \\127.0.0.1\FSA0123abcd shape was added, and the regex is unchanged.

cases.test_name: eng/rules-harness/plants.json rows S01-S04 (Cancel never abandons the scan thread)

After rule 1 became content patterns: clean baseline CLEAN (xUnit 7 Facts, Fitness 25 rules). 40 rows, 40 AS-RECORDED, 0 stray hits: F01-F16, P07c-e, S01-S08 and D1-D13.

tests.note: Intended mutant detection: exit 1, S02 MISSED-BY-FITNESS (not DIVERGENCE-CLOSED), which proves the judge() change. The yaml was restored from a backup and its hash checked equal. I deleted the scratch copies the harness kept.
The C-025 command: 4 rows AS-RECORDED, exit 0.
H-001 and H-002 both passed. Details are in O-027 and O-032.

tests.note: 155 passed, 0 failed. That is 149 before, minus 3 folded facts, plus 6 Theory rows, 2 facts and 1 InlineData. RuleCopiesAgreeTests passes on the reconciled yaml.
Returned 13 ms after Cancel, no wait line, final line present.

tests.command: taad3.fitness.check(<worktree>) under the engine's venv, no code graph built
tests.note: Verdict pass: 25 rules, 0 violations, 0 unmatched, 0 unran, 57 files. It now passes without CodeGraph op=rebuild.
AGREE 7 facts <- 10 twinned entries, 21 patterns; 15 settled entries.

tests.command: git diff --name-only eafb1c3 -- <the staleness path list>
tests.note: Only tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/Rig/SmbRig.cs changed, and git hash-object gives 8fdf6e87345668eafc91b09015bdf83997820801, the named exempt blob.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case All -IncludeNetwork; eng/dotnet.ps1 test ... --filter Network=SMB-LOOPBACK
tests.note: The person-run network check. Under the design's contract no stage runs it: it creates and removes SMB mappings. N-001..N-004 passed in the person's run at eafb1c3 and stay valid under the staleness rule. StalledShareTests has never run on the extracted rig.

deviations: Rule 1 ('the stopping wording is a pure function of elapsed time') bans System.Windows, System.IO and Microsoft.Win32 with the content pattern \b(?:System\.Windows|System\.IO|Microsoft\.Win32)\b. The design and O-035 said must_not_import. The import form cannot be measured wherever no code graph exists: eng/rules-harness exited 2 on its clean baseline ('fitness rules that did not run'), so it had measured nothing since eafb1c3. The design's own 'because' also notes the rule is UNRAN until CodeGraph op=rebuild. The content pattern is at least as strict, since it also catches fully-qualified names and aliases, and plants S05 to S08 prove it fires.

The staleness rule's one exemption names SmbRig.cs by content blob (8fdf6e87345668eafc91b09015bdf83997820801), not by a commit SHA as M2's disposition said. The builder may not commit, and the engine's commit of this attempt also carries non-listed files, so no single-purpose commit SHA exists for me to record. `git rev-parse <HEAD>:tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/Rig/SmbRig.cs` is just as mechanical a check and pins the exact content.

The armed-hook cases for O-027 and O-032 live in a new tests/window/HookCases.ps1, not in WindowCases.ps1. WindowCases.ps1 is wholly on the staleness list, and editing it would have made the person's N-001..N-004 pass stale. The design meant SmbRig.cs's comment to be the only listed-path change. HookCases.ps1 loads WindowCases.ps1's helpers and settings by name from its parse tree, so nothing is copied, and a helper that disappears fails loudly.

In eng/rules-harness/harness.py (SL-031's tool), judge() reports DIVERGENCE-CLOSED only for divergence rows. Without this, a Fitness miss on a settled-rule plant, where xUnit quiet and Fitness fire are expected, would be labelled as a closed divergence with advice to delete a divergences.json row.

In .taad/fitness.yaml I merged the engine's second SL-038 block with build 1's into one block. For rules 2 to 4 I kept design 2's texts verbatim. I dropped build 1's superseded entries: 'Cancel does not abandon the scan thread' and the three 'only the rig changes the machine's SMB mappings' entries. Design 2's patterns are case-sensitive on 'net use' and have no \b on the cmdlet names, which is slightly looser than build 1's. I renamed build 1's eng entry to match design 2's naming.
not_built: Nothing in the obligations was left undone. What remains is person-run by contract. StalledShareTests (C-024) has never run on the extracted rig. N-001..N-004 (C-016, C-019, C-023) passed at eafb1c3 in the person's run and were not re-run.
follow_ups: A person runs StalledShareTests (`eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj --filter Network=SMB-LOOPBACK`, about 70 s) at the new HEAD. It has never run since the rig moved to Rig/SmbRig.cs, and the network-check record is incomplete without it.
Fold HookCases.ps1's H-001 and H-002 into WindowCases.ps1 the next time WindowCases.ps1 has to change anyway, since that change makes the network pass stale regardless.

WindowCases.ps1's Get-RigMappings matches rig mappings case-insensitively (-match), while LoopbackShare.IsRigMapping has a case-sensitive 'fsa' prefix. It only reads mappings, so nothing is deleted wrongly, but align it to -cmatch when WindowCases.ps1 is next changed.

Engine: when a design attempt renames rules, the rules it appends land as a second '# settled by' block next to the earlier attempt's, which gave duplicates here: 28 rules for 5 intents. It also did not append design 2's rule 1, because the name already existed.

eng/rules-harness went unable to measure (exit 2) as soon as a settled import rule was declared, and no gate ran it. Any gate that accepts an architecture_rules change could run `harness.py --scenario clean` to catch this.
Engine: any settled must_not_import rule is UNRAN at a gate that has not built a code graph. Either gates build the graph, or designs should prefer content patterns.
